healthcareSystem: Government provides free basic healthcare to all including tourists. However, facilities are limited, especially outside Thimphu. The Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) covers basic healthcare for tourists.
qualityNotes: Healthcare infrastructure is limited throughout Bhutan. Thimphu and Paro have the best facilities. Rural areas have basic health units. Complex medical cases are referred to hospitals in India (typically Kolkata, Guwahati, or Delhi). Altitude sickness is a significant risk for trekkers.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 9am-6pm weekdays. Limited hours on weekends. Very few pharmacies outside Thimphu and Paro. Hospital pharmacies may be the only option in rural areas.
pharmacyTips: Bring all necessary medications from home. Pharmacy stock in Bhutan is limited and many common Western brands may not be available. The government imports medications but selection is narrow. Stock up before trekking.
prescriptionRules: Bhutan has relatively informal prescription practices. Available medications can often be purchased at hospital pharmacies. Limited selection means many specific drugs are unavailable.

restrictedMeds.name: Opioid medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Carry doctor's documentation and original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Bring documentation. Bhutan has strict drug policies.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Illegal in Bhutan. Do not bring any cannabis-related products.

bringDocumentation: Carry a comprehensive doctor's letter for all medications. Bring enough supply for your entire trip plus extra — specific medications may be impossible to find in Bhutan. Altitude sickness medication (acetazolamide/Diamox) should be brought from home.

travelInsurance.tips: Strongly recommended with medical evacuation coverage. Helicopter evacuation from trekking areas is extremely expensive. Ensure coverage for high-altitude trekking if applicable. Basic healthcare is free but facilities are limited — evacuation to India may be necessary for serious conditions.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations unless arriving from a yellow fever endemic country (proof of yellow fever vaccination required in that case). Malaria prophylaxis recommended for southern lowland areas.

waterNotes: Do not drink tap water anywhere in Bhutan. Bottled water is available in towns. Boil, filter, or treat water in rural areas and during treks. Hotels in Thimphu and Paro usually provide safe drinking water.
foodSafetyTips: Bhutanese food is chili-heavy — ema datshi (chili cheese) is the national dish. Food in established restaurants and hotels is generally safe. Be cautious with raw vegetables and unpeeled fruit. Stick to well-cooked foods in rural areas. Altitude can reduce appetite.
medicalTourismNote: Bhutan is not a medical tourism destination. Patients requiring specialized care are typically sent to India.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Bhutan. Emergency numbers, hospital info, altitude sickness advice, vaccinations, and travel insurance for trekking.

hospitals.name: Jigme Dorji Wangchuck National Referral Hospital (JDWNRH)
hospitals.notes: Bhutan's largest and best-equipped hospital. Emergency services 24/7. English widely spoken. The primary hospital for tourists.

hospitals.name: Paro General Hospital
hospitals.nearTouristArea: Paro (near the airport and Tiger's Nest)
hospitals.notes: Main hospital near the international airport. Basic but adequate for emergencies. English spoken.

hospitals.name: Punakha District Hospital
hospitals.notes: District hospital serving the Punakha valley. Basic facilities. Can handle minor emergencies.

hospitals.name: Bumthang District Hospital
hospitals.notes: Small district hospital. Basic services. Serious cases transferred to Thimphu.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Very limited. Basic dental services at JDWNRH in Thimphu. No specialized dental clinics for tourists.
dentalCare.costRange: Free at government hospitals (basic services). Private options essentially nonexistent.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is very basic. Handle any dental work before traveling to Bhutan. Emergency extractions can be done at the national hospital.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, go to JDWNRH in Thimphu. If in a remote area, you may need to travel to Thimphu or return to your home country for proper care.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. Bhutan has few mental health professionals. JDWNRH has a psychiatric unit.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are in early development in Bhutan. The country has been increasing focus on mental well-being but professional services are scarce. Online therapy is the most practical option for travelers.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Bhutan has very limited accessibility infrastructure. The mountainous terrain, steep steps at monasteries and dzongs, and unpaved paths present significant challenges for mobility-impaired travelers.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: JDWNRH in Thimphu has some accessibility. Other hospitals have limited accommodation.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Roads are winding mountain roads. No wheelchair-accessible public transport. Private vehicles with drivers are the norm for tourists.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Many key sites like Tiger's Nest monastery require strenuous hiking. Discuss accessibility needs with your tour operator before booking. Thimphu and Paro towns are more manageable. All tourists must book through a licensed operator.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Limited testing available at JDWNRH in Thimphu.
covidStatus.notes: Bhutan has lifted all COVID-related entry restrictions. The Sustainable Development Fee applies to all tourists.

insuranceClaimProcess: Government hospitals provide basic receipts. Documentation may be informal. Private insurance claims may require additional supporting documentation. Keep all records. Your tour operator can assist with medical documentation.

commonCosts.note: Basic healthcare is free for tourists in Bhutan's government hospitals. The Sustainable Development Fee ($100/night) partially covers this. However, facilities are limited and complex care may require expensive evacuation to India.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation insurance is essential. Helicopter evacuation from trekking areas to Paro can cost $5,000-15,000. Air ambulance from Paro to India adds significant cost. Druk Air operates the only international flights from Paro.
